title: Valorization of insect frass for biogas production
text:
In this lecture, we will explore the valorization of insect frass (i.e. the residual material from insect bioconversion processes) as a co-substrate for biomethane production. The session covers the intersection of circular economy principles, waste-to-energy systems, and sustainable bioprocessing technologies.

Key Topics:

Insect frass composition and characteristics relevant for biomethanization
Anaerobic co-digestion for enhanced biogas production
Process optimization strategies: Pretreatment methods, co-digestion with other organic substrates, retention time and temperature considerations
Current challenges and opportunities: Scale-up limitations, regulatory frameworks, integration with insect farming systems, economic potential


Learning outcomes: By the end of this lecture, you will have an understanding of how insect frass can be integrated into circular bioeconomy systems, be able to evaluate different bioprocessing technologies for frass valorization, and assess the feasibility of frass-based bioenergy production.

title: Thomas Klammsteiner
text: I am a microbiologist specializing in microbial ecology, with a strong focus on microbiome research related to digestion and microbe-host interactions. I am broadly interested in biological data science and apply advanced analytical approaches to better understand complex biological systems. Through my research, I aim to contribute new insights and practical solutions that bridge fundamental science and real-world applications.
